entities.summary: Obesity: A growing medical condition in which individuals have an excess of body fat, resulting in various health complications and affecting individuals globally. First described by the ancient Greek physician Hippocrates in the 5th century BCE, obesity has become a significant public health concern over the centuries. The Roman naturalist Pliny the Elder (23-79 CE) documented the relationship between diet, lifestyle, and weight gain, while the Greek physician Galen (129-216 CE) proposed that an overabundance of food and drink led to a sluggish metabolism. In the 17th century, the French physician Jean-Baptiste Le Maire (1687-1745) conducted the first recorded scientific study on obesity, using a combination of observation, experimentation, and mathematical calculations. Le Maire's work laid the groundwork for modern understanding of obesity and its consequences. Today, obesity is recognized as a major risk factor for chronic diseases, including heart disease, diabetes, and certain types of cancer. The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that over 39% of adults worldwide have obesity, with significant regional and socioeconomic disparities. As a result, obesity has become a pressing global health concern, necessitating multifaceted approaches to prevention, treatment, and policy-making.
